filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.question: In Philippians 1:18, Paul rejoices as long as Christ is proclaimed.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.learningObjective: Observe the cause of Paul's joy.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.feedbackCorrect: By pretext or by truth, Christ proclaimed makes Paul rejoice.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Philippians 1:18: in this I rejoice, he says.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.hint: See the condition of his joy.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.question: In Philippians 1:21, tap who Paul's living is.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.learningObjective: Identify the center of Paul's life.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.feedbackCorrect: For him, to live is not a project: it is a person.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the verb; who fills the living comes after.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what dying is for him, not living.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.hint: Look for the name after the verb "é".

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-03.question: According to Philippians 1:21, what does Paul say about living and dying?
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-03.feedbackCorrect: Both halves turn on Christ, not on fear.

feedbackWrong.a: He is sure about both sides of the sentence.
feedbackWrong.b: Dying, for him, is gain, not any kind of failure.
feedbackWrong.d: He does not flee: he judges staying more necessary.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-03.hint: Compare the two halves of the verse.

options.a: To live is uncertain, and to die is to forget
options.b: To live is to suffer, and to die is to fail
options.c: To live is Christ, and to die is gain
options.d: To live is to flee, and to die is to lose all

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.question: Put Philippians 1:20 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence of Paul's hope.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.feedbackCorrect: No shame, Christ exalted, in life or in death.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the hope of not being put to shame.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.hint: The sentence closes with life and death.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.question: In Philippians 1:18, what does Paul do when Christ is proclaimed, even by pretext?
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.learningObjective: Remember Paul's reaction to the proclamation.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.feedbackCorrect: Christ's proclamation makes Paul rejoice, however it comes.

feedbackWrong.a: He does not fight over the motive: he celebrates the news.
feedbackWrong.b: Tears do not appear: he says he will keep rejoicing.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.hint: It is his reaction to the gospel announced.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.question: What does Philippians 1:18 communicate that connects to this context?
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.learningObjective: Link Paul's joy to the proclamation of Christ.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.feedbackCorrect: Even in prison, he rejoices: the announcement keeps going.

feedbackWrong.b: He does not rage: he says he will keep rejoicing.
feedbackWrong.c: The gospel advances; no end is announced here.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.hint: See his reaction to Christ being announced.

options.b: Anger at those who preach differently
options.c: Sadness at the end of the gospel

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.question: In Philippians 1:23–24, Paul decided to depart because staying in the flesh no longer served the church.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.learningObjective: Understand the dilemma between departing and staying.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.feedbackCorrect: He desires to depart, but judges staying more necessary for them.

feedbackWrong.true: The desire is to depart; his judgment is to stay for their sake.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.hint: Separate his desire from his judgment.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-02.question: In Philippians 1:23, tap the word that shows what Paul feels about departing.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-02.feedbackCorrect: He feels desire to depart and be with Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: He is the destination of the desire, not the word of feeling.
feedbackWrong.c: That names his tension, not the desire itself.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-02.hint: Look for the verb "sinto" and what comes after.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.question: How does Paul's joy relate to his future in Philippians 1:18–19?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.learningObjective: Relate present joy and future hope.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.feedbackCorrect: Present joy and trust in prayer and the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.a: He trusts prayer and the Spirit, not rivals.
feedbackWrong.b: He already rejoices, in prison, before any release.
feedbackWrong.c: Fear does not rule: there is expectation and hope in him.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.hint: Join today's joy with his hope.

options.a: He leaves the future in his rivals' hands
options.b: He will only rejoice after leaving prison
options.c: He trades joy for fear of judgment
options.d: He rejoices now and trusts the church's prayer

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.question: How do Paul's thoughts connect in Philippians 1:23–24?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.learningObjective: Understand the chain of Paul's dilemma.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.feedbackCorrect: Desire, recognition, and judgment for others: that is the order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the desire he feels.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.hint: The judgment for the church closes the reasoning.

options.a: He desires to depart and be with Christ
options.b: He recognizes that departing would be far better
options.c: He judges staying more necessary for the church

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-05.question: In Philippians 1:24, how does Paul evaluate staying in the flesh for the church's sake?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-05.feedbackCorrect: The church's good weighs more than his desire.

feedbackWrong.a: Shame is exactly what he hopes not to have.
feedbackWrong.b: He sees fruit and need in staying, not uselessness.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-05.hint: It is a judgment about others' good.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.question: What links Philippians 1:23 to 2 Corinthians 5:8?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.learningObjective: Relate Paul's desire in two letters.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, to depart is to be present with the Lord.

feedbackWrong.a: There is no fear: there is desire and trust in both.
feedbackWrong.b: The mission continues; the shared point is being with him.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.hint: Compare the destination of departing in both texts.

options.b: End of the mission on earth
options.c: Desire to be with the Lord

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-01.question: Philippians 1:21 shows death without being final loss, because living and dying turn on Christ.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-01.feedbackCorrect: Christ is the center of both sides: life and death.

feedbackWrong.false: He calls dying gain, not final loss.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-01.hint: See what occupies the center of the sentence.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.question: In Philippians 1:20, tap where Christ will be exalted, according to Paul.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text where Christ is exalted.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.feedbackCorrect: Alive or dead, his body is Christ's stage.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the manner of proclamation, not its place.
feedbackWrong.b: That is his feeling, not where Christ appears.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.hint: Look for the place after "engrandecido no".

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.question: What reading do Philippians 1:20–21 support about Paul's life?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.feedbackCorrect: In both outcomes, what matters is Christ exalted.

feedbackWrong.b: He does not measure success by release: Christ is the measure.
feedbackWrong.c: Staying is a judgment of love for the church, not lack of faith.
feedbackWrong.d: He calls dying gain, not failure.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.hint: See what is the same in his life and death.

options.a: Christ is the center in life and also in death
options.b: Success is leaving prison at any cost
options.c: Staying alive proves he lacked faith to depart
options.d: Dying would be the total failure of the gospel

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.question: What sequence reveals the sense of Philippians 1:18–23?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.learningObjective: See Christ as the thread of the whole passage.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.feedbackCorrect: From proclamation to being with Christ: the thread is the same name.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with joy at the proclamation in prison.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.hint: Being with Christ is the arrival point.

options.a: Christ proclaimed makes imprisoned Paul rejoice
options.b: Christ exalted in him, alive or dead
options.c: Being with Christ is the best destination

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.question: In Philippians 1:21, what does Paul say dying is for him?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries Paul's hope.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.feedbackCorrect: Being with Christ makes death gain, not loss.

feedbackWrong.b: Loss is the opposite of what he declares here.
feedbackWrong.c: Punishment does not appear: he speaks of being with Christ.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.hint: It is a word from the world of gains.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.question: What links Philippians 1:20 to Galatians 2:20?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.learningObjective: Link "to live is Christ" to the faith of Galatians.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.feedbackCorrect: In Galatians, Paul says the same: I no longer live; Christ lives.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts put Christ right at the center of life.
feedbackWrong.c: The law is not the declared center in these verses.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.hint: See who lives, according to both texts.

options.a: Life without Christ at the center
options.c: Law as the center of life

estudo:fp-01-alegria.context: Paul writes from prison, unsure if he will leave alive. Some preach Christ even from twisted motives, and the church in Philippi prays for him. Even so, the letter's tone is joy, not complaint.
estudo:fp-01-alegria.focusQuestion: What would still be joy for you if everything else were taken away?
estudo:fp-01-alegria.keywordGloss: In Paul, joy does not depend on circumstances: it comes from Christ being proclaimed and exalted.
facts: Paul rejoices as long as Christ is proclaimed, by pretext or by truth.
He expects deliverance thanks to the church's prayer and the Spirit's provision.
Christ will be exalted in Paul's body, by life or by death.
For Paul, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
He desires to depart and be with Christ, which is incomparably better.
He judges it more necessary to stay in the flesh for the church's sake.
